summary: Meeting card shows the next meeting at a glance: a countdown, the meeting on a short time track with a now line creeping toward it, and the call's join link with a copy button. When the start time arrives the countdown says so and the meeting turns live. It suits an assistant that keeps people on time for their calls.
use: When a home screen or sidebar should show the next call and how long until it starts
When an assistant reminds a person about a meeting and offers the link in one place
When people often need to copy a call link to share it in chat
When a calendar view is too much and one upcoming meeting is all that matters
features: The countdown follows `now`: "In 30 minutes", "In 1 minute", then "Starting now" at the `start` time and "Ended" after `end`. Pass `status` to write your own line.
The time track runs from half an hour before `start` to half an hour after `end` unless you set `from` and `to`, with ticks every 15 minutes and taller ones on the hour.
The meeting sits on the track in the accent tint with its length inside, and the now line moves to `now` with a short glide each time it changes.
From `start` until `end` the meeting is live: a ring in the accent goes round it, and the dot beside the countdown pulses.
The join line shows the service's mark, "Join on Google Meet" and the link. `provider` and `mark` change the service, and `onJoin` replaces opening the link in a new tab.
The copy button puts the full link on the clipboard, turns into a check and says "Copied" for a moment, and calls `onCopy`.
a11y: Join and copy are native buttons, reachable with Tab and pressed with Enter or Space; the copy button is named by `copyLabel`.
The time track is one image to screen readers, labelled with the time now and when the meeting runs, so the ticks and axis are not read one by one.
With reduced motion the dot stops pulsing and the now line jumps to its place instead of gliding.

faq.q: How do I keep the countdown live?
faq.a: Pass the current time as `now` and update it once a minute from your own clock, for example with a `setInterval`. The countdown, the now line and the live state all follow it.

faq.q: Can I use it for Zoom or Teams?
faq.a: Yes. Set `provider` to the service's name and pass its logo as `mark`. The join line then reads "Join on" and that name, and the link and copy button work the same.

faq.q: What time format does it expect?
faq.a: 24-hour "HH:MM" strings for `start`, `end`, `now`, `from` and `to`, like "10:30". The axis shows them as you pass them.
